summary: Prolonged chat cold-start (TTFB) and intermittent 504s in multi-turn sessions following serving stack transition
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth reports a sustained increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions and occasional 504s in long multi-turn conversations starting ~2025-11-04 02:00 UTC. The degradation coincided with the regional rollout of the 2025-11 serving stack transition (runtime v2.4 + kernel optimizer) and a model repin to rwi-7b-v2 for lower latency.

Impact:
- Elevated p50/p95 TTFB for chat completion API calls from ~220ms / 420ms to ~1.1s / 3.8s for affected sessions.
- Intermittent 504s observed on ~2-3% of requests in us-west during peak.
- Customer reports user-facing slowdowns in AtlasHealth's in-app chat assistant; production SLA risk.

Environment:
- Prod, region: us-west primary (also spikes seen in eu-central).
- Customer on enterprise tenant with model pinned to rwi-7b-v2 and fallback to openlm-3b-quant.
- Serving stack: runtime v2.4 rolled 2025-11-04 01:30 UTC with kernel optimizer alpha enabled.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a long-running chat session (8+ turns) using the chat completions endpoint.
2) Send short prompt payloads (~20-40 tokens).
3) Observe increased latency for the first token of the assistant response; sometimes receive 504.

Observed behavior:
- Cold sessions and model handoffs show elevated initial stall before first token emission (~900ms - 4s).
- Streaming remains healthy after first token in many cases, but some sessions fail with connection resets/504 before any tokens.

Expected behavior:
- TTFB consistent with historical baseline (~200-400ms) and <0.5% 5xx rate.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided request IDs and timestamps (attached to ticket).
- Links to SLO dashboard heatmaps and p95 latency graphs included in related_confluence_pages.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Support (Maya): Acknowledged with customer, requested sample request IDs and logs for the affected time window. Escalated to SRE. First response ETA 24h.

2025-11-05 - Customer (AtlasHealth - DevOps): Provided request IDs: rwd-cc-20251104-0832-{redacted}, rwd-cc-20251104-0921-{redacted}. Noted impact highest between 02:20-04:10 UTC. Asking for quick mitigation while you investigate.

2025-11-05 - SRE (Ethan): Collected traces for supplied request IDs. Initial observation: increased queue wait times on router and repeated model container cold-start spikes when sessions are routed to new runtime variant.

2025-11-06 - Eng (Nikhil Patel): Kernel optimizer telemetry shows higher compile-time stalls for short-sequence workloads under the new execution path; warmup success rate dropped to 78% vs baseline 96% in us-west during rollout window.
2025-11-06 - Support (Maya): Communicated interim mitigation to customer: pinned their tenant to the pre-rollout runtime variant for us-west; asked to verify if TTFB recovered.
2025-11-06 - Customer (AtlasHealth): Confirmed immediate improvement after pin: p50 TTFB returned to ~260ms; 504s ceased. Customer requests permanent fix and postmortem.
2025-11-07 - Eng (Ethan): Currently preparing rollback and a targeted patch to optimizer heuristics. Planning follow-up postmortem and runbook updates for future rollouts.

2025-11-07 - Support (Maya): Notified customer of planned rollback to runtime v2.3 in us-west tonight with expected maintenance window and no impact to other regions. Will follow up with postmortem link when available.
investigation_notes: Traces: For request rwd-cc-20251104-0832-{redacted} the trace shows router queuing spike of 780ms and container cold-start ~1.1s before the first token generation call reached the model process.

Metrics: p50/p95 TTFB (customer tenant slice) before rollout (2025-11-03): 220ms / 410ms. After rollout (2025-11-04 02:00-05:00): 1.1s / 3.8s. 5xx rate rose from 0.2% to 2.6% in us-west for short payload chat completions.

Hypothesis 1: Kernel optimizer's just-in-time compilation path increases overhead for short sequences, causing cold-start and handoff stalls. Evidence: compile-time histograms show ~850ms median compile time for small sequences under optimizer flag.

Hypothesis 2: Router affinity policy combined with new runtime variant leads to higher cache miss rates (prefix/KV cache) on model handoff. Evidence: prefix cache hit rate dropped from 94% to 61% in affected timeslots.

Short-term workaround validated: pinning tenant to pre-rollout runtime variant eliminated regression for customer.

Logs and links:
- SLO dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/atlashealth-ttfb
- Trace example: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/rwd-cc-20251104-0832
- Kernel optimizer telemetry: https://internal.redwood.ai/telemetry/kernel-optimizer/2025-11-04
resolution: Immediate mitigation: Pinned AtlasHealth's tenant to runtime v2.3 in us-west on 2025-11-06 23:10 UTC; customer confirmed recovery of TTFB and elimination of 504s.

Root cause (preliminary): Combination of a new kernel optimizer compilation path and router affinity changes introduced during the 2025-11 rollout increased cold-start overhead for short-sequence chat workloads and reduced effective prefix cache hits during model handoffs.

Permanent fix plan: Roll back runtime v2.4 in us-west, ship a patch to kernel optimizer to skip JIT compile for short sequences or leverage precompiled kernels, and adjust router affinity policy to better preserve warm model containers across handoffs. Target deploy: 2025-11-09 after validation in staging.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to be published to Confluence and linked to this ticket.
- Update runtime rollout runbook to include short-sequence regression tests and a warmup verification step.
- Add canary gating on prefix cache hit rate and compile-time histograms during future rollouts.
- Notify affected enterprise customers of the mitigation and expected timeline for patch.
